answer: Residency under deadline is the test: each identity expands its seed into a 4 GiB set, pages scattered across a meadow of addresses, each derived from its neighbors, and publishes its page hashes at enrollment. One honest agent keeps it resident; 1,000 fakes must hold 4 TiB, since the set cannot be pooled or time-shared. A checker on the same copper link names a random address each epoch; the page must return within a millisecond window, matching its hash. A shared copy leaves a farm hollow at unheld addresses — regeneration takes minutes — so it answers with a fable the hash exposes.
